newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says pilgrimage quota system still in force.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says pilgrimage quota system still in force.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said on Sunday Moslem countries should continue to abide by a quota system governing the number of pilgrims performing the annual haj pilgrimage and denied it has made any exceptions.
Saudi Pilgrimage and Endownments Minister Mahmmoud bin Mohammad Safar said Moslem countries should continue to adhere to the quota "which aims to safeguard the interests and safety of pilgrims."

"The reasons behind (the quota system) still exist...I deny talk of exceptions...The kingdom is keen that everybody abide by the quota and there are no exceptions," the official Saudi Press Agency quoted him as saying.
The denial appeared aimed at Iran which in December said Saudi Arabia has agreed to allow 100,000 Iranian pilgrims at this year's haj which falls in mid-April, up from 60,000.

The number of pilgrims performing the haj to Mecca and Medina every year is governed by quotas agreed in 1988 by the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) which sets them in relation to the country's population.
Saudi Arabia says the aim of the quota system is to ease congestion during the haj which often attracts more than two million Moslems, half of them from outside the country.
Saudi newspapers said on Sunday more than 700,000 pilgrims have already arrived in the kingdom by land, sea and air.
Iran has for years objected to the quota system by the Jeddah-based OIC, which groups most of the world's Moslem countries, and said it was a Saudi pretext to limit the number of Iranian pilgrims.

Normally tense relations between the two regional giants usually fall to new lows during the haj season in a row over a the quota and Tehran's insistence on holding political rallies mainly directed against the United States and Israel in defiance of a Saudi ban.
Iran boycotted the haj for three years after some 400 people, mainly Iranian pilgrims, were killed in clashes in 1987 between security forces and Iranians holding a political rally.
